statement.summary: Theorem 8.1 is frozen as three independent Props, one per clause: `irrevStabStatement` (Stab(s) ≤ Stab(Φ s)), `irrevVecStatement` (s ∈ S(v) → Φ s ∈ S(v) for v ≠ 0) and `irrevSetStatement` (Φ '' S ⊆ S); `irrevStatement` is their conjunction. Φ ranges over every map Config → Config with `Equivariant Φ`, the translation-equivariance of Definition 2.4.
deltas: Alphabet Σ is `Fin σ`; the claim is invariant under relabelling the alphabet.
Standing hypotheses n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1, σ ≥ 2 (Definition 2.1) are carried as explicit antecedents; the conclusions do not use them.

'Translation-equivariant (Definition 2.4)' is the `Equivariant` predicate on an arbitrary global map, not the offset form `caMap`; every offset CA is equivariant (`caMap_equivariant`), so this is the more general reading.
Stab(Φ(s)) ⊇ Stab(s) is written `stab s ≤ stab (Φ s)` (order of the subgroup lattice).
Φ(S_{n^d}) is the set image `Φ '' SS n d σ`.
The 'in particular' consequences are frozen as separate conjuncts, not derived inside the statement.

maps.label: Φ translation-equivariant

lean.text: ∀ Φ : Config n d (Fin σ) → Config n d (Fin σ), Equivariant Φ →

maps.note: Φ is an arbitrary global map with the equivariance property; the same binder occurs in all three Props.

maps.label: Φ(τ_v s) = τ_v Φ(s)

lean.text: ∀ (v : Lat n d) (s : Config n d A), Φ (shift v s) = shift v (Φ s)

maps.note: Definition 2.4's equivariance, verbatim, for all v.

maps.label: τ_v s (u) = s(u+v)
maps.note: Same sign convention as the paper.

maps.label: Stab(Φ(s)) ⊇ Stab(s)
maps.note: ⊇ read right-to-left as ≤ in the lattice of additive subgroups (which is set inclusion of carriers).

maps.label: Stab(s)
maps.note: Stab(s) is the subgroup with carrier {v | τ_v s = s} (`stab`, Definitions.lean). (The TeX anchor includes the ⊇ to keep the line break of the official PDF.)

maps.label: for every configuration s

lean.text: ∀ s : Config n d (Fin σ), stab s

maps.note: Configurations are functions Lat n d → Fin σ.

maps.label: s ∈ S(v) ⇒ Φ(s) ∈ S(v)

lean.text: s ∈ SV v → Φ s ∈ SV v

maps.note: Per-vector form; the paper's 'in particular' is not a hypothesis — the Lean conjunct is stated (and proved) on its own.

maps.label: v ≠ 0 (domain of S(v))
maps.note: Definition 2.3 defines S_{n^d}(v) only for v ≠ 0; Lean carries v ≠ 0 explicitly (the implication would hold for v = 0 too).

maps.label: S_{n^d}(v) = {s : τ_v s = s}
maps.note: The first expression of Definition 2.3; its identification with Fix(⟨v⟩) is not used here.

maps.label: Φ(S_{n^d}) ⊆ S_{n^d}

lean.text: Φ '' SS n d σ ⊆ SS n d σ

maps.note: Φ(S) is the set image `Φ '' S`.

maps.label: S_{n^d} = ⋃_{v≠0} S_{n^d}(v)

lean.text: ∃ v : Lat n d, v ≠ 0 ∧ shift v s = s

maps.note: Membership in SS is ∃ v ≠ 0 with τ_v s = s, literally membership in the union.

maps.label: the three clauses as one statement
maps.note: Lean freezes the main claim and both 'in particular' consequences as independent conjuncts.

maps.label: standing hypotheses n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1, σ ≥ 2
maps.note: From Definition 2.1; carried explicitly although the conclusion needs none of them (non-counting statement, so σ ≥ 2).

maps.label: alphabet Σ = Fin σ

lean.text: Φ : Config n d (Fin σ) → Config n d (Fin σ)

maps.note: Only |Σ| matters; the core lemma `stab_le_stab_apply` is proved for an arbitrary alphabet type A.
